items.headline: Can you have a backyard fire pit in Burlington?.
items.deck: A wood fire for sitting around is generally not allowed in urban Burlington. Propane and cooking fires are treated differently.
items.label: Home rules
items.alt: Illustration comparing a wood fire pit with a propane fire table in a Burlington backyard.
items.storyGoal: Explain the Burlington backyard-fire rule in plain language, including the urban wood-fire ban, cooking exception, propane and natural-gas exception, and rural permit system.
items.rawHeadline: Can you have a backyard fire pit in Burlington?
items.shortHeadline: Can you have a backyard fire pit in Burlington?.

items.headline: Do you need a permit for a shed in Burlington?.
items.deck: Not always. The building-permit threshold is 15 square metres, but a small shed still has to follow zoning rules.
items.label: Home rules
items.alt: Illustration of a backyard shed with measurement lines and a 15-square-metre permit threshold.
items.storyGoal: Answer the Burlington shed-permit question directly, then separate the 15-square-metre building-permit exemption from zoning and property-specific approvals.
items.rawHeadline: Do you need a permit for a shed in Burlington?
items.shortHeadline: Do you need a permit for a shed in Burlington?.
